The Global 7500, originally named the Global 7000, made its first flight on November 4, 2016, was [[type certified]] by [[Transport Canada]] on September 28, 2018, and entered service on 20 December 2018. The Global 7500 is a clean sheet design{{cite web |last1=Whelan |first1=Ian |title=Bombardier's New Global 7000 Business Jet Debuts |url=https://bjtonline.com/business-jet-news/bombardiers-new-global-7000-business-jet-debuts |website=Business Jet Traveler |date=24 October 2017 |publisher=AIN Media Group, Inc. |access-date=6 December 2024}} with a new [[transonic wing]] and is the first purpose built business jet featuring a four-zone cabin.{{cite web |last1=Lynch |first1=Kerry |title=Bombardier: 'Right Resources' in Place for Global 7000 |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2015-11-03/bombardier-right-resources-place-global-7000 |website=Aviation International News |publisher=AIN Media Group, Inc. |access-date=6 December 2024}} The Global 7500 has a range of {{cvt|7,700|nmi|mi km}} and is the largest business jet in the world. The Global 8000 was initially a shorter, three-zone aircraft but was updated in May 2022 as a four-zone jet similar to the Global 7500, reaching {{Convert|8000|nmi|mi km}} and with a top speed of Mach 0.95 ({{Convert|729|mph|kn km/h|abbr=on|disp=or}}), making it the fastest business jet and fastest civilian aircraft since [[Concorde]]. The Global 8000, also has a [[cabin altitude]] of {{Convert|2691|ft|m}} while flying at {{Convert|41000|ft|m|abbr=out}}, the lowest cabin altitude of any business jet in production.{{Cite web |date=2025-11-04 |title=Bombardier Global 8000 Sets Cabin Altitude Record |url=https://www.flyingmag.com/bombardier-global-8000-sets-cabin-altitude-record/ |access-date=2025-11-07 |website=www.flyingmag.com |language=en-US}} The Global 8000 was introduced in 2025. == Development == Announced in October 2010, the jets were initially scheduled for introduction in 2016 for the Global 7500 and 2017 for the Global 8000. In 2015, Bombardier decided to redesign the aircraft's wing, a change that, in conjunction with other design challenges, delayed the programme by over two years.{{cite news |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/transport-canada-registers-first-global-7000-429014/ |title=Transport Canada registers first Global 7000 |work=[[FlightGlobal]] |date=5 September 2016}} The goal of the redesign was to reduce the wing's weight without altering its aerodynamic profile. The aircraft [[fly-by-wire]] system architecture is based on that of the [[CSeries]].{{cite news |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/weight-reduction-cited-for-global-7000-wing-redesign-434265/ |title=Weight reduction cited for Global 7000 wing redesign |work=[[FlightGlobal]] |date=16 February 2017}} The airframe will use [[aluminium–lithium alloys]] like the other airliner. The program cost more than US$1 billion.{{cite news |url=https://www.thestar.com/business/2010/10/19/bombardiers_new_business_jet_program_to_cost_more_than_1b.html |title=Bombardier's new business jet program to cost more than $1B |first=Ross |last=Marowits |work=[[The Canadian Press]] |date=October 19, 2010}} === Bombardier Global 7500 === [[File:Static display, EBACE 2018, Le Grand-Saconnex (BL7C0585).jpg|thumb|The 7500 fuselage is {{cvt|11|ft|3|in|m}}, longer than the original Global Express]] Formerly named Global 7000, its entry into service was initially scheduled for 2016.{{cite press release |url=https://www.bombardier.com/en/media/newsList/details.749-bombardier-grows-its-flagship-global-family-with-two-new-jets-the-global-7000-and-global-8000-aircraft.bombardiercom.html |title=Bombardier Grows Its Flagship Global Family with Two New Jets: the Global 7000 and Global 8000 Aircraft |publisher=[[Bombardier Aviation]] |date=October 16, 2010}} Former [[Formula One]] driver and long time Bombardier brand ambassador [[Niki Lauda]] announced his order ahead of the [[European Business Aviation Association#Annual event: EBACE|EBACE]] 2015 convention.{{cite press release |url=https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2015/05/17/1504994/0/en/Formula-1-Champion-Niki-Lauda-Purchases-New-Bombardier-Global-7000-Aircraft.html |title=Formula 1 Champion Niki Lauda Purchases New Bombardier Global 7000 Aircraft |publisher=[[GlobeNewswire]] |date=17 May 2015}} The first test aircraft underwent taxi testing in October 2016.{{cite news |url=https://aviationweek.com/shownews/nbaa/bombardiers-global-7000-fly-soon |title=Bombardier's Global 7000 To Fly Soon |date=November 1, 2016 |work=[[Aviation Week & Space Technology]]}} Dedicated to testing basic system functionality and assessing the handling and [[flying qualities]] of the aircraft, its maiden flight was performed on November 4, 2016, climbing to 20,000 feet (6,096 m) and reaching {{convert|240|kn|mph}} during the 2 h 27 min flight.{{cite press release |url=https://businessaircraft.bombardier.com/en/news/global-7000-aircraft-completes-first-flight |title=Bombardier Global 7000 Aircraft Successfully Completes First Flight |date=November 4, 2016 |publisher=[[Bombardier Aviation]]}} The production wing was in final design in February 2017.{{cite news |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2017-02-16/first-global-7000-logs-100-hours-ftv2-fly-soon |title=First Global 7000 Logs 100 Hours; FTV2 To Fly Soon |first=Chad |last=Trautvetter |date=February 16, 2017 |work=[[Aviation International News]]}} FTV2 flew on March 6, 2017, "The Powerhouse" is designed to test aircraft systems, including propulsion, electrical and mechanical systems.{{cite press release |url=https://www.bombardier.com/en/media/newsList/details.bba-20170306-second-bombardier-global-7000-flight-test-vehicle-t.bombardiercom.html |title=Second Bombardier Global 7000 Flight Test Vehicle Takes to the Skies |date=March 6, 2017 |publisher=[[Bombardier Aviation]]}} FTV1 is used to open the performance envelope and reached Mach 0.995 on March 29, 2017.{{cite press release |url=https://www.bombardier.com/en/media/newsList/details.bba_20170329_need-for-speed-propels-global-7000-aircraft-to-mach.bombardiercom.html |title=Need for Speed Propels Global 7000 Aircraft to Mach 0.995 in Early Flight Testing |publisher=[[Bombardier Aviation]] |date=March 29, 2017}} FTV3 flew on May 10, 2017, "The Navigator" will be used to test the [[avionics]] and electrical system performance.{{cite press release |url=https://www.bombardier.com/en/media/newsList/details.bba-20170510-global7000ftv3firstflight.bombardiercom.html |title=Bombardier Global 7000 Flight Test Program Ramps Up with Maiden Flight of Third Flight Test Vehicle |date=May 10, 2017 |publisher=[[Bombardier Aviation]]}} By the end of May 2017, the three prototypes flew a combined 250 hours.{{cite news |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/bombardier-and-triumph-resolve-global-7000-wing-disp-437753/ |title=Bombardier and Triumph resolve Global 7000 wing dispute |date=31 May 2017 |work=[[FlightGlobal]] |first=Kate |last=Sarsfield}} The fourth prototype, used for cabin interior validation, is called "The Architect" and the fifth and final, for the entry-into-service, is called "The Masterpiece".{{cite news |url=https://aviationweek.com/shownews/ebace/bombardier-plays-name-test-aircraft |title=Bombardier Plays 'Name That Test Aircraft' |date=May 22, 2017 |first=Molly |last=McMillin |work=[[Aviation Week & Space Technology]]}} The fifth has a slightly lighter production wing supplied by the [[Triumph Group]], after a dispute over the wing weight was resolved.{{cite news |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2017-06-13/bombardier-new-lighter-wing-wont-delay-global-7000 |title=Bombardier: New Lighter Wing Won't Delay Global 7000 |first=Kerry |last=Lynch |date=June 13, 2017}} [[File:General Electric Passport tested at Arnold Air Force Base Engineering Development Complex.jpg|thumb|[[GE Passport]] tested at [[AEDC]]]] By mid-July 2017, the three flight-test aircraft had accumulated 500 hours.{{cite news |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2017-08-08/faa-issues-special-conditions-global-7000-alloy |title=FAA Issues Special Conditions for Global 7000 Alloy |first=Kerry |last=Lynch |date=August 8, 2017 |work=[[Aviation International News]]}} On 15 August 2017, after "high vibration and high inter-turbine temperature readings", the second prototype's right [[GE Passport]] had an in-flight [[flameout]] at FL410 and the aircraft went back to [[Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport|Wichita Airport]] 156 nmi (290 km) away for a single engine landing.{{cite news |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/global-7000-test-aircraft-suffers-in-flight-engine-f-440426/ |title=Global 7000 test aircraft suffers in-flight engine flameout |date=18 August 2017 |work=[[FlightGlobal]] |first=Kate |last=Sarsfield}} By October 2017, the four flight-test aircraft had flown 900 hours.{{cite news |url=https://aviationweek.com/shownews/nbaa/bombardier-shows-global-7000 |title=Bombardier Shows Off Global 7000 |date=October 10, 2017 |first1=Molly |last1=McMillin |first2=Fred |last2=George |work=Aviation Week Network}} In April 2018, the flight test campaign surpassed 1,800 hours and confirmed a range increase from {{cvt|7,400|to|7,700|nmi|mi km}}, greater than the competing [[Gulfstream G650]]ER's {{cvt|7,500|nmi|mi km}}, but still overshadowed by the smaller Global 8000's range of {{cvt|7,900|nmi|mi km}}, {{cvt|200|nmi|mi km}} more than the Global 7500.{{cite news |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/global-7000-claims-longest-range-title-for-business-447705/ |title=Global 7000 claims longest range title for business jets |date=16 April 2018 |first=Stephen |last=Trimble |work=[[FlightGlobal]]}} As the original [[Bombardier Global Express|Global Express]] is developed into the Global 5500 and 6500, it is renamed Global 7500 to reflect this range increase.{{cite press release |url=https://www.bombardier.com/content/bombardiercom/en/media/newsList/details.bba_20180528_bombardier-elevates-the-name-of-its-flagship-busine.bombardiercom.html |title=Bombardier Elevates the Name of its Flagship Business Jet to the Global 7500 Aircraft as Performance Continues to Exceed Expectations |date=May 28, 2018 |publisher=Bombardier}} By the end of May 2018, the five flight-test aircraft had amassed about 2,000 hours towards the type's planned entry-into-service at year-end.{{cite news |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2018-05-28/longer-legs-bombardier-flagship-becomes-g7500 |title=With Longer Legs, Bombardier Flagship Becomes G7500 |first=Kerry |last=Lynch |date=May 28, 2018 |work=Aviation International News}} By June 2018, 2,300 flight test hours had been completed by the test fleet towards certification. The first production aircraft entered the completion centre in May 2018.{{cite press release |url=https://www.bombardier.com/content/bombardiercom/en/media/newsList/details.bba_20180614_bombardiers-global-7500-jets-begin-arriving-in-mont.bombardiercom.html |title=Bombardier's Global 7500 Jets Begin Arriving in Montreal as On-Schedule Ramp-Up Continues and Program Surpasses 2,300 Flight Test Hours |date=June 14, 2018 |publisher=Bombardier}} [[File:Bombardier Global 7500, Paris Air Show 2019, Le Bourget (SIAE8902) (cropped).jpg|thumb|The Global 7500 bedroom]] Flight testing was completed by August 2018 after over 2,400 hours; [[type certification]] and introduction into service are expected by year-end, with 15-20 customer deliveries in 2019, as 20 aircraft were in final assembly.{{cite news |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2018-08-02/bombardier-completes-global-7500-flight-testing |title=Bombardier Completes Global 7500 Flight Testing |first=Chad |last=Trautvetter |date=August 2, 2018 |work=Aviation International News}} By September 2018, the test aircraft had flown over 2,700 hours as FTV1 was retired from testing and repainted to be used as a demonstrator.{{cite news |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2018-09-07/bombardier-mission-accomplished-global-7500-ftv1 |title=Bombardier: 'Mission Accomplished' for Global 7500 FTV1 |first=Chad |last=Trautvetter |date=September 7, 2018 |work=Aviation International News}} Bombardier was expecting certification in September 2018.{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bombardier-businessjets/bombardier-expects-global-7500-jet-certification-this-month-sources-idUSKCN1LX2HH |date=September 17, 2018 |title=Bombardier expects Global 7500 jet certification this month: sources |first=Allison |last=Lampert |work=[[Reuters]]}} [[Transport Canada]] awarded its type certification on September 28, 2018.{{cite press release |url=https://www.bombardier.com/content/bombardiercom/en/media/newsList/details.bba_20180928_global-7500-aircraft--industrys-longest-range-busin.bombardiercom.html |title=Global 7500 Aircraft, Industry's Longest Range Business Jet, Awarded Transport Canada Type Certification |date=September 28, 2018 |publisher=Bombardier}} FAA type certification followed on November 7, 2018.{{cite press release |url=https://www.bombardier.com/en/media/newsList/details.bba_20181107_bombardiers-award-winning-global-7500-business-jet-.bombardiercom.html |title=Bombardier's Award-winning Global 7500 Business Jet Earns FAA Approval and Continues to Move Towards Entry-into-service this Year |date=November 7, 2018 |publisher=Bombardier}} The first was expected to be delivered in December, then 15 to 20 in 2019, and 35 to 40 in 2020, with the program sold out through 2021.{{cite news |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2018-12-07/bombardier-preps-7500-delivery-coming-days |title=Bombardier Preps For 7500 Delivery 'In Coming Days' |first=Kerry |last=Lynch |date=December 7, 2018 |work=AIN online}} After being delivered in early December, the Global 7500 entered service on 20 December with 100 secured orders.{{cite news |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/bombardier-global-7500-enters-service-454591/ |title=Bombardier Global 7500 enters service |date=20 December 2018 |work=[[FlightGlobal]] |first=Kate |last=Sarsfield}} In February 2019, Bombardier acquired the Global 7500 wing manufacturing program and facilities from [[Triumph Group]].{{cite press release |url=https://www.bombardier.com/en/media/newsList/details.binc-20190206-bombardier-completes-acquisition-of-global-7500-ai.bombardiercom.html? |title=Bombardier completes acquisition of Global 7500 aircraft wing program |publisher=[[Bombardier Aerospace]] |date=February 6, 2019}} In 2023, its equipped price was $78M.{{cite news |url= https://infogram.com/bca-table-2023-jets-ultra-long-range-1ho16vorwrqkx4n |title= Purchase planning handbook - Ultra long-range Jets table |date= Second Quarter 2023 |work= Business & Commercial Aircraft}} In Aug 2024, Bombardier announced that the Global 7500 business jet had achieved over 50 speed records within a span of less than 50 weeks.{{Cite web |title=Bombardier's Global 7500 Sets More Than 50 Speed Records In 50 Weeks {{!}} Aviation Week Network |author=Molly McMillin |work=aviationweek.com |date=21 August 2024 |access-date=19 March 2025 |url= https://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/aircraft-propulsion/bombardiers-global-7500-sets-more-50-speed-records-50-weeks}} In November 2024, the company announced that the Global 7500 aircraft had set its 75th speed record.{{cite web |last1=McMillin |first1=Molly |title=Bombardier Global 7500 Gathers More Than 75 Speed Records |url=https://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/aircraft-propulsion/bombardier-global-7500-gathers-more-75-speed-records |website=Aviation Week |publisher=Informa Markets |access-date=6 December 2024}} In March 2025, Bombardier marked a major achievement for its flagship business jet, the Global 7500, announcing it had reached an impressive 100 officially recognized speed records. Since its service entry in 2018, in addition to its long range and a four-zone cabin layout, the Global 7500 has proven it can connect distant city pairs faster than other jets in its class, placing it among the strongest performers in business aviation. === Bombardier Global 8000 === Entry into service was initially scheduled for 2017. By September 2016, it was delayed to early 2019. Trading nearly {{cvt|8|feet}} of cabin space for {{cvt|600|nmi|mi km}} of range, the Global 8000 accounted for a very small part of the backlog in December 2017 and its schedule was expected to be determined after the Global 7500 entered service. Lacking [[Differentiation (marketing)|differentiation]], it might be replaced by a higher [[maximum take-off weight]] (MTOW) Global 7500 variant with more range.{{cite news |url= https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2018-01-03/global-7000-track-questions-remain-8000 |title=Global 7000 On Track, Questions Remain on 8000 |first=Chad |last=Trautvetter |date=January 3, 2018 |work=[[AINonline]]}} The 8000 unit cost was $71 million in 2014.{{cite web |url=https://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/bombardier-sees-strong-start-global-70008000 |title=Bombardier Sees Strong Start For Global 7000/8000 |date=May 22, 2014 |first=Fred |last=George |work=[[Aviation Week & Space Technology]]}} Instead of the initially planned 2.6 m (8.5 ft) shrink of the Global 7000, Bombardier launched the Global 8000 as a longer range variant of the Global 7500 at the May 2022 [[EBACE]]. As service entry is planned for 2025, the earlier model will be phased out for the new Global 8000, while existing Global 7500s can be retrofitted through a [[service bulletin]]. Bombardier was already flight testing its modified FTV5 testbed, which reached [[supersonic]] Mach 1.015 in May 2021; the certification campaign is expected to be completed using a single prototype. With low development costs, it will compete with the new [[Gulfstream G800]] and [[Dassault Falcon 10X]].{{cite news |url= https://www.flightglobal.com/ebace-2022/bombardier-launches-ultra-long-range-global-8000-with-supersonic-test-campaign/148756.article |title= Bombardier launches ultra-long-range Global 8000 with supersonic test campaign |author= Dominic Perry |date= 23 May 2022 |work= FlightGlobal}} In 2023, its equipped price was $81M. The first prototype made its 7.1 hr maiden flight during May 2023.{{cite news |url= https://www.flightglobal.com/business-aviation/first-global-8000-prototype-flies-71h-mission-on-maiden-sortie/153434.article |title= First Global 8000 prototype flies 7.1h mission on maiden sortie |author= Dominic Perry |date= 24 May 2023 |work= FlightGlobal}} The first Global 8000 was delivered in December 2025.{{Cite web |last=Morrison |first=Murdo |title=Bombardier hands over first Global 8000 |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/business-aviation/bombardier-hands-over-first-global-8000/165617.article |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Flight Global |language=en}}{{Cite web |author= Stefan, Teodor |title=Bombardier's Global 8000 enters into service |website= Aeronews Global |url=https://aeronewsglobal.com/bombardiers-global-8000-enters-into-service/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |language=en-US}} == Design == [[File:Bd700 (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|The Global 7500 and Global 8000 are part of the company's Global family of aircraft that also includes the Global 5500 and Global 6500 aircraft]] Both the Global 7500 and Global 8000 feature the same [[transonic]] wing.{{cite news |url=https://aviationweek.com/shownews/nbaa/ultra-long-range-jets-about-enter-market |title=Ultra-Long Range Jets About To Enter The Market |work=[[Aviation Week & Space Technology]] |date=November 2, 2016}} They are powered by the [[General Electric Passport]] 20 {{convert|18,920|lbf|kN|abbr=on}} thrust engine with reduced [[NOx]] emissions and 8% better [[fuel efficiency]] than the Global Express XRS, allowing a Mach 0.90 high-speed cruise. As part of its effort to make the long-range aircraft comfortable for the passengers, Bombardier developed a new [[ergonomic]] [[Airline seat|passenger seat]], called the ''Nuage''. The seat design took seven years to complete.{{cite news |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2018-04-30/bombardier-global-7000-seats-bring-cloud-comfort |title=Bombardier: Global 7000 Seats Bring Cloud-like Comfort | first=Matt | last=Thurber |date=April 30, 2018 |work=AIN Online}} Airbus-owned [[Stelia Aerospace]] supplies the main fuselage.{{cite news |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/analysis-why-global-7500-is-key-to-bombardiers-fut-455861/ |title=Why Global 7500 is key to Bombardier's future |date=27 February 2019 | first=Dominic | last=Perry |work=[[FlightGlobal]]}} The new, larger and lower-drag wing is optimized for Mach 0.85 with a 35.3° quarter chord [[wing sweep]], a thinner [[thickness-to-chord ratio]], leaner flap track [[aircraft fairing|fairings]], improved [[lift-to-drag]] performance, more efficient [[winglet]]s and up to 30% better low-speed lift due to double-slotted, inboard [[Fowler flaps]]. The new [[fly-by-wire]] flight controls with active load alleviation and the flexible, relatively highly loaded wing damps [[Clear-air turbulence|turbulence]]. The metal [[airframe]] uses [[aluminium–lithium alloy]]s to save weight. It shares the same fuselage diameter with older Global models, but has thinner frames, which increase the cabin width and height by {{cvt|1|in}}. Additionally the {{cvt|300|sqin|dm2}} cabin windows are 80% larger, the nose cowl is recontoured, and the aft fuselage and empennage are both new designs. The basic [[aircraft maintenance checks|inspection intervals]] are 850 hours or 36 months, with C checks are every 12 years or 8,500 cycles and a limit of 17,000 cycles before life extension through intensive maintenance is required. === Bombardier Global 7500 === [[File:Bombardier Global 7500 on static display, EBACE 2018, Le Grand-Saconnex (BL7C0578).jpg|thumb|The Global 7500 flight test vehicle at [[EBACE]] in 2018]] The Global 7500 cabin is one-third longer than competing models, providing a fourth seating section up from three, can sleep eight passengers and offers an optional shower and a sleeping crew rest area. Bombardier marketing focuses on ultra-[[high-net-worth individual]]s. Despite the wing area being smaller than the [[Gulfstream G650ER]] and a 11% higher MTOW, it has lower [[V speeds]] and better runway performance due to the high-lift system with [[leading-edge slats]] and double-slotted flaps for a similar power loading. Hourly fuel flow per engine is {{cvt|500|lb}} at idle, {{cvt|6,240|lb}} at takeoff, {{cvt|1,280 to 1,370|lb}} in cruise at Mach 0.85/{{cvt|484|kn|mph km/h}} TAS, {{cvt|1,730|lb}} at Mach 0.9/{{cvt|515|kn|mph km/h}} TAS and {{cvt|2,400|lb}} at Mach 0.925/{{cvt|523|kn|mph km/h}} TAS, around {{cvt|75,000|lb}} and ISA conditions. An even longer range variant could reach {{cvt|1,000|nmi|mi km}} more with another {{cvt|8,000|lb}} of fuel. === Bombardier Global 8000 === [[File:Global8000.jpg|thumb|The initial, smaller Global 8000 will now have the same cabin length as the company’s four zone Global 7500 jet]] The initial BD-700-2A13, marketed as the Global 8000, was to be {{convert|2|ft|3|in|m|abbr=on}} longer than the Global Express. It was to feature a three-zone 2,236 cu.ft. (63.32 cu.m.) cabin and a range of 7,900 nmi (14,631 km) at Mach 0.85, farther than any other existing business jet. At the 2022 European Business Aviation Conference and Exhibition, Bombardier announced that the Global 8000 would feature the same cabin length as the company’s Global 7500 aircraft with a range of 8,000 nmi (14,800 km) and reach a maximum speed of Mach 0.95. The Global 8000 is currently the fastest civilian aircraft since Concorde and the fastest business jet in the world.{{cite web |last1=Bundy |first1=Brent |title=Bombardier introduces new flagship bizjet, the Global 8000 |url=https://skiesmag.com/news/bombardier-introduces-new-flagship-global-8000-aircraft/ |website=Skies Mag |publisher=MHM Publishing Inc. |access-date=6 December 2024}} The Global 8000 is available as an upgrade to existing Global 7500 aircraft or as production baseline (serial 70240, 70250 and subsequent), incorporated flight envelope expansion from M.925 to M.950, thrust increase of up to 7%, fuel volume increase, reduced cabin altitude, Environmental Control System (ECS) flow reduction, and changes to the avionics including automatic ADS selection.{{Cite web |title=FSBR BD-700-2A12 Rev 6 |url=https://www.faa.gov/aircraft/draft_docs/fsb/FSBR_BD-700-2A12_Rev_6_Draft.pdf}}{{Cite web |title=Bombardier Selling Global 7500 To 8000 Conversion Package {{!}} Aviation Week |url=https://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/aircraft-propulsion/bombardier-selling-global-7500-8000-conversion-package |access-date=2026-06-06 |website=aviationweek.com}} == Operational history == In March 2019, a Global 7500 set the record for the longest mission ever flown by a purpose-built business jet, with a {{cvt|8152|nmi|mi km|adj=on}}, 16-hour flight from [[Singapore Changi Airport|Singapore]] to [[Tucson International Airport|Tucson, Arizona]]; the aircraft landed with fuel reserves for nearly 1.5 hours of additional flight.{{cite press release |title=Bombardier Global 7500 Aircraft Completes the World's Longest Range Business Jet Flight in History |url=https://www.bombardier.com/en/media/newsList/details.binc-20190304-bombardier-global-7500-aircraft-completes-the-worl.bombardiercom.html |publisher= Bombardier |date=4 March 2019}} On 6 October 2019 Bombardier improved their longest mission with an {{cvt|8225|nmi|mi km|adj=on}} non-stop flight between Sydney and Detroit, claiming the record for "the longest city-pair flown by a purpose-built business aircraft".{{cite news |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/global-7500-breaks-business-aircraft-range-record-461346/|title=Global 7500 breaks business aircraft range record |work=[[Flight Global]] |date=9 October 2019}} The Global 7500 also broke the business jet speed record for a flight from [[Van Nuys Airport]] near Los Angeles to [[Teterboro Airport]] near New York in under four hours, cruising at Mach 0.925 for much of the flight.{{cite press release | title=Bombardier's Global 7500 Aircraft Breaks Key Speed Record Between Los Angeles and New York |url=https://businessaircraft.bombardier.com/en/news/bombardiers-global-7500-aircraft-breaks-key-speed-record-between-los-angeles-and-new-york |publisher=Bombardier |date=27 March 2019}} In May 2019, a Global 7500 completed the longest ever non-stop flight from [[London City Airport]], taking off from the airport's 4,948 ft runway and flying to Van Nuys Airport with the equivalent weight of a fully fitted interior and 2,400 lbs of additional payload.{{Cite web |title=Bombardier’s Global 7500 Jet Demonstrates Unmatched Performance with Industry’s First Ever Non-stop Mission from London City Airport to Los Angeles |url=https://bombardier.com/en/media/news/bombardiers-global-7500-jet-demonstrates-unmatched-performance-industrys-first-ever-non}} == Operators == While Bombardier is not publishing a specific backlog, industry analyst Rolland Vincent estimated that 200 orders had accumulated by the time of the first flight in November 2016, mostly for the 7500 version.{{cite news |url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2016-11-04/bombardiers-flagship-global-7000-takes-sky |title=Bombardier's Flagship Global 7000 Takes To The Sky | first=Kerry | last=Lynch |work=Aviation International News |date=November 4, 2016}} Including the [[Bombardier Global Express|Global 5500/6500]], Bombardier expects to deliver 90–100 Globals a year by 2021, up from 40 in 2018, with four 7500 a month, and higher if needed. Luxury charter [[VistaJet]] signed a deal to purchase up to 30 units; [[NetJets]], the largest [[fractional jet]] provider, will take up to 20 Global 7500s and Hong Kong management firm HK Bellawings Jet has 18 Global 6500/7500s orders and options.{{cite news |url=https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/analysis-bombardier-ready-to-seize-high-ground-with-452355/ |title=ANALYSIS: Bombardier ready to seize high ground with Global 7500 |date=2 October 2018 | first=Kate | last=Sarsfield | work=[[FlightGlobal]]}} The Global 7500 had 100 secured orders as it entered service on 20 December 2018. In October 2019, VistaJet said it plans to launch commercial flights on its first Global 7500 in January 2020. Bombardier considered 2020 a successful year for the Global 7500 as they delivered 35 aircraft to various customers, and on 29 March 2021, the company marked the milestone delivery of the 50th Global 7500.{{Cite web|title=Bombardier Marks 50th Global 7500 Aircraft Delivery Milestone|url=https://bombardier.com/en/media/news/bombardier-marks-50th-global-7500-aircraft-delivery-milestone|access-date=2021-05-13|website=Bombardier|language=en}} As of 6 December 2024, the company delivered its 200th Global 7500.{{cite press release |url=https://bombardier.com/en/media/news/bombardier-celebrates-200th-delivery-its-industry-defining-global-7500-aircraft |title=Bombardier Celebrates 200th Delivery of its Industry-Defining Global 7500 Aircraft, Underscoring Success of this Record-Setting Ultra-Long-Range Platform | publisher=[[Bombardier Aviation]] |date=9 December 2024}} In November 2022, NetJets was named as the fleet launch customer for the Global 8000. The company paid US$312M in a firm order for four Global 8000s and also converted existing orders for eight Global 7500s to 8000s. NetJets plans to convert its current fleet of Global 7500s to a 24 aircraft fleet of Global 8000s.{{cite web|url= https://www.avweb.com/aviation-news/business-aviation-news/bombardier-names-launch-customer-for-global-8000/|title= Bombardier Names Launch Customer For Global 8000|access-date= 2 December 2022|last= O'Connor|first= Kate|work= AVweb|date= 2 December 2022|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20221202125836/https://avweb.com/aviation-news/business-aviation-news/bombardier-names-launch-customer-for-global-8000/|archive-date= 2 December 2022|url-status= live}} {| class="wikitable" |+ Known orders |- !
